questions.q: What does the Create Accounting process actually do?
options: It deletes accounting events that are no longer needed
It applies the active accounting method's AADs and rules to eligible accounting events, producing subledger journal entries
It defines a new Chart of Accounts
It only generates reports, with no effect on journal entries
questions.explain: Create Accounting is the process that executes everything configured in Chapters 1-3 against real accounting events, producing journal entries.

questions.q: What can you do with journal entries produced in Draft mode?
options: Transfer them immediately to the General Ledger
Review them (lines, accounts, amounts, descriptions), but they cannot be transferred to GL and are not permanent
Nothing; Draft mode produces no visible output at all
Only a system administrator can ever view them
questions.explain: Draft mode produces reviewable, non-permanent journal entries that cannot yet be transferred to the General Ledger.

questions.q: What happens when you re-run Create Accounting in Draft mode for the same event?
options: It creates a duplicate, permanent journal entry every time
The new draft run simply replaces the previous draft for that event, with no downstream risk
It automatically transfers the entry to the General Ledger
It is not possible to re-run Draft mode at all
questions.explain: Draft runs can be repeated freely; each new draft replaces the prior one, making experimentation safe.

questions.q: What distinguishes Final mode from Draft mode?
options: Final mode produces entries that are permanent and become eligible for transfer to the General Ledger
Final mode is identical to Draft mode in every way
Final mode can be freely re-run and simply overwrites the prior entry
Final mode never produces any journal entries
questions.explain: Final mode locks in the journal entry as the official subledger accounting record and makes it eligible for transfer to GL.

questions.q: What is the standard pattern many companies follow when using Create Accounting?
options: Run Final mode exclusively, skipping Draft mode entirely
Run Draft mode first to review the accounting safely, then run Final mode once satisfied, often on a schedule like nightly or at period-end
Alternate randomly between Draft and Final with no particular order
Only run Create Accounting once per year
questions.explain: The Draft-then-Final pattern lets consultants and accountants review accounting safely before committing to the permanent Final version.
